"""Browser authentication-state boundary."""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import secrets
import time

from .sessions import SessionStore

_session_store = SessionStore()


def _sign(session_id: str, secret: str) -> str:
    return hmac.new(secret.encode(), session_id.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def create_browser_auth_state(user_id: str, secret: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    session_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    _session_store.save(session_id, {"user_id": user_id, "created_at": time.time()})

    cookie_value = f"{session_id}.{_sign(session_id, secret)}"
    return {
        "name": "session_id",
        "value": cookie_value,
        "httponly": True,
        "secure": True,
        "samesite": "Lax",
        "path": "/",
    }

---
name: adr-auth-cookies
description: Auth state must use signed HTTP-only cookies, never JWT/bearer tokens in browser storage
metadata:
  type: project
---

ADR-AUTH: Authentication state uses signed HTTP-only cookies (session id + HMAC signature), not JWTs held client-side.

**Why:** Project decision (ADR-AUTH) to avoid XSS-exposed browser storage of credentials.
**How to apply:** When implementing or touching login/auth flows (e.g. `src/auth.py`), issue an opaque signed session-id cookie (`httponly`, `secure`, `samesite`) rather than a JWT or any token in `localStorage`. Pairs with [[adr-storage-sqlite]] for where the session payload itself lives.

---
name: adr-storage-sqlite
description: User sessions are persisted in SQLite, not Postgres or any external database
metadata:
  type: project
---

ADR-STORAGE: Persist user sessions in SQLite (stdlib `sqlite3`), no Postgres, no `psycopg2`, no external database server.

**Why:** Project decision (ADR-STORAGE) to keep session persistence self-contained without an external DB dependency.
**How to apply:** When implementing session storage (e.g. `src/sessions.py`'s `SessionStore`), use `sqlite3` against a local db file. Do not introduce Postgres/psycopg2 or other external database clients. Pairs with [[adr-auth-cookies]] which references the session id stored here.

- [ADR-AUTH](adr_auth_cookies.md) — auth state uses signed HTTP-only cookies, never JWT/localStorage tokens
- [ADR-STORAGE](adr_storage_sqlite.md) — sessions persisted in SQLite, no Postgres/psycopg2/external DB
